# Ambient ocean and engine audio

`public/audio/ocean-engine.v1.wav` is an original procedural sound design by
Ocean Drive project contributors, generated by `scripts/build-ambient-sound.ts`
on 2026-10-06. No recordings, samples, external services or third-party audio
were used. The generated audio is dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0
(https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/). The generator remains a
project source contribution under the repository's terms.

Rebuild with `bun scripts/build-ambient-sound.ts`, then record its SHA-256 with
`bun run assets:record`. The fixed seed produces filtered periodic noise for
soft ocean wash and phase-modulated 55/110/165 Hz harmonics for a distant engine.
All modulation completes integer cycles, and filters use periodic initial
conditions. PCM has no codec padding; Web Audio loops the decoded buffer.

The file is 288,044 bytes (12 seconds, 12 kHz mono, 16-bit PCM), below the
320 KiB optional audio budget exported from `lib/production-budgets.ts`.
It is never preloaded. First enable fetches and decodes once; subsequent toggles
reuse the buffer. Playback gain is 0.22 with a 350 ms linear fade in/out.
The AudioContext suspends after fade-out; disposal aborts a pending fetch and
closes the context. Gain automation reaches silence even if hidden-tab timers
are throttled.

The preference uses `sessionStorage` key `ocean-drive:sound:v1`, with an in-memory
fallback if storage is refused. A fresh tab starts silent. Reading mode and
hidden tabs preserve preference while suspending sound. Returning resumes only
while enabled. Reload restores preference; browser autoplay policy may require
the next gesture before the enabled loop can resume. Load/decode failures reset
the toggle and announce a short Portuguese retry message.

Before release, listen on headphones and a phone speaker for at least two full
loops, including fades, visibility changes and reading-mode transitions.
Automated seam/level checks do not replace that listening assessment.
